method: Live GitHub star-sorted queries, relevance screening, direct comparable metadata, current docs/representative code and recent issue/PR reads. Highest-star relevant found is bounded by query coverage, not a global ranking.

briefs.user: Web developers debugging which cookie reaches a route
briefs.pain: Same cookie names at several domains and paths obscure why a request sees different state.
briefs.capability: Explain host-only/domain, slash-boundary path and secure eligibility for each supplied cookie and request.
briefs.alternatives: Browser DevTools, Requests cookie jars, curl and Tough Cookie
briefs.limits: Only already-normalized cookie records: no Set-Cookie parsing, public suffix list, SameSite, expiry, partitioning, prefix acceptance, IDNA or browser conformance. IDs must not contain cookie values. URLs and domains remain visible in local output.

briefs.user: DNS operators reviewing a zone rollout across authoritative servers
briefs.pain: Ordinary numeric comparison mishandles SOA serial rollover, while a partial rollout can look complete.
briefs.capability: Classify equal, ahead, behind, half-range ambiguous and unavailable observations; calculate an explicit equality quorum.
briefs.alternatives: BIND utilities, dnspython serial arithmetic, checkzoneserial
briefs.limits: No live DNS queries, DNSSEC verification, TTL or propagation-time inference. Input is a single manually supplied authoritative-server snapshot. Server labels are asserted unique, not verified identities. RFC 1982 half-range ordering is undefined; ahead does not count as expected equality.

briefs.user: Package maintainers inspecting alternatives in a license expression
briefs.pain: Nested AND/OR expressions make the syntactic alternatives difficult to review without expanding them manually.
briefs.capability: Enumerate bounded conjunction alternatives, applying AND precedence, parentheses and atomic WITH exceptions.
briefs.limits: SPDX-style syntax, not a validated SPDX license registry. Unknown identifiers are retained; case is preserved; deprecated IDs are not normalized. No legal interpretation, compatibility, compliance, policy selection or license-text detection. Enumeration is bounded and deliberately fails when expansion exceeds limits.

briefs.user: Linux service authors reviewing an explicit startup transaction offline
briefs.pain: Requires/Wants pull in units but do not order them; After/Before order units but do not pull them in.
briefs.capability: Expand explicit pull-ins from roots, separately construct ordering edges and return one concrete cycle or deterministic topological order.
briefs.limits: Normalized JSON snapshot, not a unit-file parser or replacement for systemd-analyze verify. No default/implicit dependencies, drop-ins, generators, aliases, conditions, failure propagation, stop ordering or live system operations. Missing pull-ins make complete false; inactive ordering targets are explicit. Blocked includes descendants of cycles, not just cycle members.

briefs.user: Network support engineers needing a small offline capture accounting receipt
briefs.pain: A traffic trace contains payloads and many protocols when the immediate task is per-direction captured-byte totals.
briefs.capability: Read bounded classic Ethernet/IPv4 TCP pcaps and summarize directional packet, payload, wire-byte and SYN/FIN/RST counts without outputting payload bytes.
briefs.limits: Classic pcap 2.4 only, Ethernet linktype 1, complete IPv4 TCP records. Non-IPv4, non-TCP and fragmented records are explicitly counted as skipped. No pcapng, VLAN dissection, reassembly, checksum validation, retransmission deduplication, timing performance analysis or splitting reused four-tuples into connections. Retransmissions count again. Output includes IPs and ports and is not anonymous. No live capture.
